findings.description: updateLocation drops externalCalendarId for updated events — `CalendarManager.updateEvent` never sets `externalId`, so location changes persist references without an `externalCalendarId`, and later deletes hit `primary`. Fall back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` when `result.externalId` is absent.

Video booking references lose credentialId, so meetings are never deleted on cancel — `handleCancelBooking.ts:491` has no else branch, so an undefined video `credentialId` means the Zoom/Daily/Meet meeting is never deleted on cancellation. Restore the video fallback so `createMeeting`'s `credentialId` is persisted.

Dereference of possibly undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar — `handleNewBooking` sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` and the webhooks set `[]`, so this throws a TypeError for a Google Meet booking when the organizer has no destination calendar instead of falling back to Cal Video. Guard the dereference.

Dead selectedCalendar fallback passes undefined calendarId — The `find` only runs when the predicate's value is falsy, so it never matches and `calendar.events.update` gets an undefined `calendarId`. Fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId` or match on `credentialId`.

deleteEvent destination calendar lookup always falls back to primary — The `find` can never match a falsy `externalCalendarId`, so every delete falls back to "primary" and events on secondary destination calendars are never deleted. Use the destination calendar's `externalId` as the fallback.

Collective team destination calendars dropped when organizer calendar is null — `destinationCalendar` is set to `null` a few lines above when no destination calendar exists, so the optional push silently drops every `teamDestinationCalendars` entry. Assign the merged array instead of pushing.

Hangout-link patch uses undefined calendarId when no matching destination calendar — Google Meet bookings with no matching destination calendar fail the patch and lose the updated description. Apply the same `|| "primary"` fallback to the `calendar.events.patch` call.

Recurring cancellation repeats deletes for each calendar reference — The recurring branch now runs once per calendar reference while still looping over credentials and `updatedBookings`, so a collective with N references deletes the same events N times. Run it once when `allRemainingBookings` is set.

Organizer email uses first destination calendar, not credential's — With `destinationCalendar` now an array of every host's calendar, an event created with host B's credential is sent with host A's email as organizer. Match the destination calendar by `credentialId` (as `selectedCalendar` does) before using its `externalId`.

addGuests updates calendar with requesting user's credentials — Calendar updates run with credentials that never created the event, so the organizer's invites are never updated when a team owner or attendee adds guests. Build `EventManager` from `booking.user`'s credentials, as the seat flow in `createNewSeat.ts` does.

addGuests handler throws unhandled P2025 when booking.userId is null — A null `booking.userId` makes id 0 throw P2025, surfacing as an unhandled 500 instead of a TRPCError. Throw an explicit TRPCError when `booking.userId` is null before querying.

isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && so team admins are wrongly denied access — `isTeamAdmin` already covers ADMIN and OWNER, so combining with `&&` reduces `isTeamAdminOrOwner` to owner-only and rejects team admins. Use `||`, or just `await isTeamAdmin(...)`.

Blacklisted guest emails bypassed via case and plus aliases — Comparing `guest` raw against lowercased `blacklistedGuestEmails` lets `Blocked@Example.com` and plus aliases bypass the blacklist, so a low-privilege attendee can inject blocked addresses. Lowercase the guest and reuse `extractBaseEmail` before comparing.

Unbounded `guests` array allows mass inserts and email fanout per request — A single caller can submit thousands of addresses, triggering as many inserts and outbound emails per request. Cap `guests` with `.max(...)` and reject oversized input.

Guest attendees can add arbitrary attendees to a booking — Any existing attendee, not just the organizer or admin, can inject arbitrary third parties into the organizer's calendar event and trigger invites without consent. Drop the `isAttendee` branch or gate attendee additions behind an organizer setting.

Guest emails are not deduplicated before createMany — `uniqueGuests` never dedupes within the incoming `guests` array, so duplicates reach `createMany` and produce duplicate rows or a constraint error. Dedupe the input server-side, since the schema has no uniqueness refinement.

sendAddGuestsEmails gets raw guests instead of the computed uniqueGuests — Passing raw `guests` makes `sendAddGuestsEmails` classify existing attendees as new, sending duplicate confirmations instead of the added-guests notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` so producer and consumer agree on what counts as a new guest.

TestMode3_Create never verifies the asynchronous legacy write — Deleting the legacy goroutine, making legacy `Create` always fail, or dropping the 10s timeout would leave this test green. Synchronize on the legacy call and assert its expectations.

Log reads TotalDocs() concurrently with watcher goroutine writes — `TotalDocs` ranges over `b.cache` without `cacheMu` while the write-event goroutine inserts into the same map, so Go raises a fatal concurrent map read and map write error at startup. Take `cacheMu.RLock()` inside `TotalDocs` or read the count only after the watcher is quiescent.

Concurrent BuildIndex calls can duplicate index construction — Concurrent callers that miss the cache for the same key now build the same index twice, with the losing index still receiving writes that are silently lost. Restore per-key serialization across the build, or check-and-insert under the lock and return the already-cached index.

Missing s.cancel() on Init failure leaks server context and watcher — A failed startup leaves an orphaned write-event watcher consuming database events for a server object nobody holds, since the context from line 229 leaks and the watcher loops keep running. Call `s.cancel()` on the error path and give `searchSupport.init`'s watch a cancellable context.

Skipping postgres case masks eager-init behavior change in resource server — This skips the only coverage of the instrumentation-server-without-http-server path on postgres, hiding that eager init in `NewResourceServer` now runs before surrounding startup state it depended on. Fix the ordering so the caller still drives initialization instead of dropping the test.

Grafana delete ability merged into canDelete but unused by menu item — In the list view `rulerRule` is undefined, so the Delete action vanishes and the merged prom ability is dead computation. Gate the menu item and `handleDelete` on the prom case too (e.g. from `promRule.uid`), or drop the unused ability merge.

Prom-only pause ability has no effect in alert list view — Because `rulerRule` is always undefined in the list view, the Pause item never renders and the merged prom pause ability has no effect. Render a pause item based on the prom rule (or remove the rulered gate) so pause works there.

Silence notifications action renders no drawer in Grafana rule list — With only `promRule` passed and `canSilence` true from the prom abilities, the `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` mount condition in RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx stays false, so the click is a silent no-op. Render the drawer from the prom rule as well.

Missing Grafana prom rule reports not loading and enables Duplicate — A missing rule reports `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported` and `Duplicate` only checks the global permission. Return `loading: true` (or not supported) when no Grafana prom rule is supplied so cloud rules don't offer Duplicate without `AlertingRuleExternalWrite`.

GrafanaRuleListItem in FilterViewResults is rendered without a key — Unkeyed, this child is reconciled by position, so per-item state like the open menu or pending identifier can attach to the wrong rule. Restore a stable key on the element, e.g. `key={key}` or `key={rule.uid}`.

Federated rule groups lose immutability in useAllRulerRuleAbilities — Passing only `rule.rulerRule` discards `rule.group`, so federated (Mimir) groups are reported as editable and the UI offers actions that cannot succeed. Keep the `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` detection on this path instead of the constant.

Non-default getShortcut() and missing validation break grant factories — A third-party grant factory predating this change aborts startup with `AbstractMethodError`, a null shortcut throws `NullPointerException` from `ConcurrentHashMap.put`, and a wrong-length shortcut makes every id it encodes unparsable. Validate `grantShortcut` for non-null and length 2 in `postInit`, and make `getShortcut()` a default method so existing implementations keep working.

testIncorrectGrantType passes on NPE and never asserts IllegalArgumentException — The fixture leaves `factory.sessionFactory` null, so the broad `catch (RuntimeException)` swallows a `NullPointerException` and the test passes without exercising the unknown-grant validation. Set a `sessionFactory` on the fixture and assert `IllegalArgumentException` specifically instead of catching `RuntimeException`.

Grant-shortcut check in isAccessTokenId is inverted — The comparison rejects ids that have the expected grant and accepts ones that do not, so every caller such as `expectCodeToToken` and `expectRefresh` fails on correct tokens and passes on wrong-grant tokens. Negate it and use `substring(4, 6)`, since the shortcut starts at index 4.

Inverted grant-type shortcut check in isAccessTokenId matcher — The inverted guard rejects a match and accepts a mismatch, so for `ac`, `dg`, `rt` and `ci` the check never triggers and `isAccessTokenId` degenerates into a UUID check. Negate it and slice `substring(4, 6)`.

isAccessTokenId matcher rejects matching grant shortcut instead of mismatching one — The matcher rejects a matching shortcut and accepts a mismatching one, so `expectCodeToToken`, `expectDeviceCodeToToken`, `expectRefresh` and `expectAuthReqIdToToken` pass for any grant value. Negate the condition and extract via `substring(4, 6)`.

Inverted access token grant-shortcut comparison in isAccessTokenId — The inverted comparison rejects a correct token and accepts any wrong grant, so the `isAccessTokenId` callers would pass even if the grant type were wrong. Negate it and use `substring(4, 6)`.

Inverted grant shortcut check in isAccessTokenId rejects correct tokens — The matcher rejects the token exactly when the encoded shortcut matches, so `isAccessTokenId(RefreshTokenGrantTypeFactory.GRANT_SHORTCUT)` and the other new expectations fail on correct tokens. Negate the condition.

isAccessTokenId extracts grant shortcut at wrong offset — The offset is off by one: the grant shortcut occupies indices 4..6, so `substring(3, 5)` yields `ta` instead of `ac` for `onrtac:…`. Slice `substring(4, 6)`.
Null check validates grantType instead of rawTokenId — Require `rawTokenId` here instead.

getSubGroupsCount may return null when cached group is unresolved — Returning null breaks the contract, and `GroupUtils` passes the value straight into `representation.setSubGroupCount(...)`, so the count can be silently absent or NPE on unboxing. Return a non-null default such as 0, or handle null in that consumer.

Reader thread not joined before asserting caught exceptions — An exception from the request in flight during the concurrent-delete window may not yet be in `caughtExceptions`, so the test can pass while the NPE still reproduces. Join the reader thread before the `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` check.

Reader thread is not joined before the exception assertion — The assertion reads `caughtExceptions` while the reader thread can still append, so a racing exception may be recorded after it passes, or the loop may exit without a read against the deleted state. Join the reader thread before `assertThat(caughtExceptions, Matchers.empty())` so every raced read counts.

Reader thread can loop forever when group deletion throws — If any `remove()` throws, `deletedAll.set(true)` is never reached and the non-daemon reader thread spins in a delay-free loop, hanging the forked JVM. Set the flag in a `finally` around the delete loop and join the thread with a bounded timeout before asserting.

Choice-format blocks hide HTML from message sanitizer — Because `normalizeValue` strips the `{n,choice,...}` block before sanitizing, HTML hidden in `error-invalid-multivalued-size` on both sides is erased and passes, enabling XSS. Sanitize the block content before substituting the placeholder instead of discarding it.

Lithuanian TOTP setup message replaced with Italian text — Lithuanian users now see an Italian sentence on the TOTP setup page. Restore a Lithuanian translation of `loginTotpStep1` here and of `totpStep1` in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/account/messages/messages_lt.properties`.

Tests never exercise allowed HTML translation branch — Both `illegalHtmlTag_en.properties` and `noHtml_de.properties` bypass the permissive branch, so breaking `containsHtml(englishValue)` would leave all tests green while legal `<b>` translations fail. Add an English/German fixture pair with an allowed tag asserting `verify()` returns empty.

Multivalued size error message uses Java MessageFormat syntax i18next cannot render — The admin console renders this key with i18next (`user-profile/utils.ts:79`), which ignores `{0}` and the `MessageFormat` choice, so users see the literal placeholder text. Keep `error-invalid-multivalued-size` in `{{n}}` form.

Missing English bundle aborts verification with raw RuntimeException — A translation file without a matching `messages_en.properties` makes `verifySafeHtml` throw a raw `RuntimeException` that escapes the `IOException` catch and aborts the build. Check `Files.exists` and report the file through `messages` instead.

All-clients grants ignored when per-client resource exists — Any client with its own resource loses the grants an admin holds on the "Clients" type resource, so all-clients `manage`, `configure` and `view` silently stop applying. Evaluate the type resource as well and fall back to it instead of consulting it only when `resourceStore.findByName` returns null.

getClientsWithPermission matches only type resource, not per-client grants — The per-client resources from `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` carry no type, so `findByType` returns only the literal "Clients" resource and omits every real grant, leaving `getRoleIdsWithPermissions` with a null client id. Iterate the realm's clients and check `hasPermission` on each instead.

canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException on token exchange path — `AbstractTokenExchangeProvider` calls `canExchangeTo` on every cross-client exchange, so enabling V2 turns each one into an uncaught exception and HTTP 500 instead of a 403. Return `false` or delegate to the existing evaluation, including the inherited 2-arg overload.

Client removal fails when both fine-grained authz features are enabled — With V1 and V2 both enabled, the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch still reaches `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` and throws, so deleting a client returns 500. Skip that branch when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is on, since V2 needs no permission cleanup.

canView(ClientModel) issues redundant per-client permission checks — `ClientsResource.getClients` calls `canView` per client, so a realm listing runs up to four resource lookups and policy evaluations each, with the type-level result never cached. Check `hasPermission(scope)` once and evaluate the client scopes in a single pass.

Missing null check on fallback resource before evaluation — When the `getResourceTypeResource` fallback also returns null, `root.evaluatePermission` dereferences a null `resource` and throws. Return `false` before the evaluation when `resource` is null.

Passkeys conditional UI include missing from base login-password.ftl — The base template behind every inheriting theme still lacks the passkey control, so passkey-only users reach a password page with no way to authenticate. Add the `<@passkeys.conditionalUIData/>` include to `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/login/login-password.ftl`.

Organization clause in shared login predicate hides linked brokers — `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` also uses `getLoginPredicate()`, so users linked to an organization IDP without `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` lose that provider from the login page. Keep the stricter predicate local to the invalidation code or add an explicit method instead of altering the shared predicate.

Login IDP cache invalidates shared entry for each new organization — Every login page then loads and copies the IDP ids of all organizations, and each new organization's first request triggers a full reload. Include `organizationId` in `cacheKeyForLogin` so entries are per-organization, or accept a per-search-key entry instead of invalidating the shared one.

Login cache test misses login-eligible IDP create/remove — Both IDPs fail `getLoginPredicate()`, so dropping the invalidation calls from `create()` and `remove()` would still pass, leaving the stale-login-list regression undetected. Add a step that creates and removes a login-eligible IDP and asserts the login caches become null for every `FetchMode`.

Discarded getForLogin results leave cached return path untested — The return half of the cached branch, resolving ids via `getById`, is never verified, so an empty or wrong returned set still passes. Collect the aliases returned by `getForLogin` and assert them against the expected set alongside the cache-entry count.

Table widget flag branch renders blank grid with empty data — Every table widget renders a blank grid once the flag is enabled, since `fields` and `result` are discarded. Feed the already-computed `result.data`, `result.meta` and `fields` into `TableWidgetVisualization`.

Error context dropped when field params are provided — Any caller passing field params gets [] for error_ids, so the new error context is silently dropped. Request the replay fields independently of the client's field list so error ids are always available.

Invalid field query param causes 500 in replay breadcrumbs — An authenticated `?field=bogus` request raises `KeyError` in `process_raw_response` and returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 400. Filter the requested fields against the known response keys before calling it.

Report tests no longer post with application/reports+json content type — Without the browser-reporting content type DRF uses the generic `JSONParser`, so these tests would still pass if `BrowserReportsJSONParser` broke. Restore `content_type="application/reports+json"` on at least one request.

Unauthenticated endpoint logs raw unvalidated report payload — This unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint lets anyone persist arbitrary content, and browser reports carry URLs, tokens and page messages into a retained warning log. Log only non-sensitive shape information instead of `raw_report`.

Replay error events mispaired by positional get_multi zip — `NodeStorage.get_multi` dedupes ids and appends cache hits after service results, so `zip` mispairs ids with another event's data and drops trailing ones. Look events up by node id instead of relying on positional order.

Mutually exclusive age/timestamp check uses truthiness, so 0 slips through — A legal value of 0 is falsy, so `timestamp`/`age` pairs like `{"timestamp": 0, "age": 5}` pass the mutually exclusive check. Use existence checks such as `"age" in self.initial_data` in `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age`.

Per-shard buffers multiply global max-flush-segments limit by process count — With N shard processes, each shard now admits ~N× the segments per cycle, so aggregate flush capacity reaches ~N × `spans.buffer.max-flush-segments` and `any_shard_at_limit` fires late, letting the queue overrun its bound. Keep the divisor global by passing the total assigned shard count to the buffer so the limit stays cluster-wide.

Spans flusher queries cluster memory once per buffer in submit — `get_memory_info()` fans out a cluster-wide `INFO` to every master regardless of `assigned_shards`, so `submit` issues one round trip per buffer and the summed totals are the same numbers counted N times. Query memory once per `submit` and reuse it across buffers.

Unhealthy flusher process is never killed due to isinstance guard — The guard never matches a `SpawnProcess`, so a hung flusher is never killed and its replacement races the old one on the same shard queues, duplicating segments and leaving orphans. Drop the `isinstance` guard or test against `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess`.

Flusher wait_produce timer uses inconsistent "shards" metric tag — The sibling `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` timers tag this same value as `shard`, so dashboards grouping on one shard tag silently miss this metric. Use `{"shard": shard_tag}` for consistency.

flusher_unhealthy tags shard with bare int instead of shard_tag — Every other emit site tags `shard` with `shard_tag`, the comma-joined group, so this metric's bare int lives in a different value domain and per-shard grouping can never match. Emit `shard_tag` here or use one identifier at all sites.

Assertion does not verify shard distribution across flusher processes — The sum equals 4 for any assignment of the shards, so the test passes even if round-robin placed them all in one process. Assert the per-process counts, e.g. sorted lengths equal `[2, 2]`.

Deadline break in join() leaves flusher processes alive — When the deadline expires, the `break` skips the `terminate()` for that process and every remaining one, leaving hung flushers running after `join()` returns. Move the terminate outside the deadline break so all spawned processes are killed on shutdown.

Sleep after drift change is a no-op due to patched time.sleep — `time.sleep` is patched to a no-op at line 15, so this returns immediately and provides none of the synchronization the comment claims, running the assertion before post-drift processing finishes. Synchronize on a real condition or remove the misleading sleep.

max_processes truthiness mishandles 0 and negative values — Truthiness treats a configured `0` as unset, silently running one process per shard instead of failing fast, while a negative value passes here and later raises `KeyError` on `process_to_shards_map`. Use an explicit None check and reject values below 1.

sync_status_outbound assignment_source unused; ExampleIntegration lacks kwargs — Status-sync cycles stay broken for the kind this PR fixes, and the first caller passing `assignment_source` will hit a `TypeError` in `ExampleIntegration.sync_status_outbound`. Update the call in `tasks/sync_status_outbound.py` and add `**kwargs` to the example integration.

AssignmentSource round-trip loses datetime type for queued — A queued `AssignmentSource` comes back with `queued` as a `str` instead of a `datetime`, and the first consumer comparing it to `timezone.now()` fails far from here. Serialize `queued` with isoformat in `to_dict` and parse it back in `from_dict`.

queued timestamp is shared across all AssignmentSource instances — Every `AssignmentSource` shares one import-time timestamp, so `queued` never reflects when that source was enqueued. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` so each instance records its own time.

Active-only Integration lookup blocks reinstalling inactive integrations — Filtering by `status=ObjectStatus.ACTIVE` makes a non-ACTIVE Integration return "Invalid installation request" even though `ensure_integration` in src/sentry/integrations/pipeline.py resets `status` to ACTIVE on reinstall. Drop the status filter so retries reach `ensure_integration`.

Pipeline state mutated before OAuth state validation — A request with a forged or invalid state still overwrites the victim's Redis-backed `installation_id` via `pipeline.bind_state`, so a later legitimate completion resolves the wrong installation in `GitHubInstallation.dispatch`. Bind `installation_id` only on the first, state-less request so rejected requests cannot mutate pipeline state.

GitHub OAuth callback state uses constant pipeline signature — `pipeline.signature` is the same constant for every user and org, so the callback check accepts any attacker-computed value and gives no CSRF protection. Generate a per-request nonce with `secrets.token_hex()`, bind it via `pipeline.bind_state`, and compare the callback against the stored value as `OAuth2LoginView`/`OAuth2CallbackView` do in src/sentry/identity/oauth2.py.

Unhandled GitHub OAuth token and user info failures return HTTP 500 — An expired code, a 401 from GitHub, or a network error escapes as an unhandled HTTP 500 instead of the error page, because `raise_for_status` in src/sentry/identity/github/provider.py and `safe_urlopen` both raise. Wrap the token request and `get_user_info` in the existing try/except and fall through to `error(request, self.active_organization)`.

KeyError when GitHub integration metadata lacks sender — `integration.metadata["sender"]` only exists for webhook-created integrations, so pipeline-created ones raise `KeyError` (HTTP 500) instead of showing the failure page; `installation.py:44` guards this same key. Read it with `(integration.metadata.get("sender") or {}).get("login")` and return `error(...)` when missing.

test_installation_not_found no longer tests installation-not-found — The second request passes a wrong `state`, so `OAuthLoginView.dispatch` returns at the state-mismatch guard and the `Integration.DoesNotExist` path is never exercised. Complete the OAuth step with the correct `pipeline.signature` state and assert "The GitHub installation could not be found."

MetricAlertDetectorHandler leaves abstract methods unimplemented — Switching `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` to `StatefulDetectorHandler` with a bare pass leaves `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values` and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` abstract, so instantiating it raises TypeError and `Detector.detector_handler` crashes for every `metric_alert_fire` detector. Implement the abstract members as no-op stubs until the metric-alert hook exists, or stop registering this class as the detector handler.

build_mock_occurrence_and_event ignores its value argument — The `value` argument is never included in the returned occurrence or event_data, so no assertion actually covers it and tests with wrong or stale values still pass. Fold `value` into what `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` returns, then pass the real evaluated value at each call site so a wrong `value` reaches the hook and fails the test.

Monitor context returns raw config, discarding mutated schedule_type — The occurrence payload keeps the raw `schedule_type` key instead of the readable label, so the copy and its replacement are wasted. Return the mutated `config` in the `"config"` field.
